title: Qnity, University of Delaware team up for semiconductor R&D, workforce
excerpt: UD Engineering has a capstone program that allows companies to recruit students. Qnity’s corporate partnership will focus on semiconductor materials research...
content_html:
This story was originally published on Manufacturing Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily Manufacturing Dive newsletter.

Qnity Electronics and the University of Delaware are collaborating to bolster the engineering talent pool and expand their research and development partnership to fuel new advanced manufacturing technologies.

UD's College of Engineering students will work with the semiconductor component maker's technical heads on academic assignments focused on addressing real-world manufacturing and operational challenges, according to the press release. UD Engineering has a capstone program that matches student teams involved in more than one academic field with corporate partners, which companies can leverage to recruit and retain workers, according to its website.

Qnity is also launching a pilot work-study program that provides students with hands-on industry experience, improving their skills while supporting automation projects.

The partnership between Qnity and UD aims to help "advance technologies and processes that are essential to the future of the semiconductor industry," CTO Randy King said in a statement. 

"By investing in hands-on learning, automation, and workforce development, we're helping build the talent and innovation ecosystem that will power the next generation of technological breakthroughs," King added.

The collaboration will also enable Qnity to work with UD faculty on semiconductor materials research and use the school's special facilities, such as the Keck Center for Advanced Microscopy and Microanalysis, to discover and evaluate manufacturing hurdles.

"[The partnership] builds sustained relationships that span the classroom, research lab, and broader UD community," Jenni Buckley, associate dean for corporate engagement and entrepreneurship at UD Engineering, said in a statement.

Qnity is expanding its R&D footprint as demand for artificial intelligence increases worldwide, in a bid to develop new technologies. The company has teamed up with global research nonprofit, Imec, to access its portfolio of research programs, according to a July 29 press release.

Qnity was formed last year when Dupont spun out its electronics business to create a new publicly traded company.

content_html_zh:
这个故事最初发表在 Manufacturing Dive 上。 要接收每日新闻和见解，请订阅我们免费的每日制造潜水时事通讯。

Qnity Electronics 和特拉华大学正在合作增强工程人才库并扩大研发合作伙伴关系，以推动新的先进制造技术。

据新闻稿称，特拉华大学工程学院的学生将与这家半导体元件制造商的技术负责人一起完成学术任务，重点是解决现实世界的制造和运营挑战。 据其网站介绍，特拉华大学工程学院有一项顶点计划，将涉及多个学术领域的学生团队与企业合作伙伴进行匹配，企业可以利用该计划来招聘和留住员工。

Qnity 还启动了一项试点勤工助学计划，为学生提供实践行业经验，提高他们的技能，同时支持自动化项目。

Qnity 和 UD 之间的合作旨在帮助“推进对半导体行业未来至关重要的技术和工艺”，首席技术官兰迪·金 (Randy King) 在一份声明中表示。

金补充道：“通过投资实践学习、自动化和劳动力发展，我们正在帮助建立人才和创新生态系统，为下一代技术突破提供动力。”

此次合作还将使 Qnity 能够与特拉华大学的教员合作进行半导体材料研究，并利用学校的特殊设施（例如凯克高级显微镜和微分析中心）来发现和评估制造障碍。

特拉华大学工程学院负责企业参与和创业的副院长珍妮·巴克利 (Jenni Buckley) 在一份声明中表示：“[此次合作]建立了跨越课堂、研究实验室和更广泛的特拉华大学社区的持续关系。”

随着全球人工智能需求的增加，Qnity 正在扩大其研发足迹，以开发新技术。 据 7 月 29 日的新闻稿称，该公司已与全球研究非营利组织 Imec 合作，获取其研究项目组合。

Qnity 成立于去年，当时杜邦公司剥离其电子业务，创建了一家新的上市公司。
